title: AWSSDK.Core
description: Core utilities and configuration shared across AWS SDK for .NET clients.

data.text: `AWSSDK.Core` provides shared configuration, logging, retry logic, and HTTP handlers used by other AWS SDK packages. You rarely add it directly, but understanding it helps when customizing AWS clients.
All AWS service clients share a common configuration pipeline. You can customize retry behavior, logging, and proxy settings via `AWSConfigs` or constructor options.

data.title: Configure AWS Retry and Logging

data.text: When you create an AWS client without explicit credentials, the SDK checks environment variables, shared credentials files, and IAM roles in order.

data.title: Credential Resolution Order
data.code:
# Environment variables
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1

# Or use the shared credentials file (~/.aws/credentials)
[default]
aws_access_key_id = AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
aws_secret_access_key = wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
region = us-east-1

terms.definition: The foundation package for all AWS SDK for .NET service clients.
The ordered set of locations the SDK checks to find AWS credentials.
Built-in logic that retries failed requests with exponential backoff.

data.title: Tip
data.text: Use IAM roles instead of static keys when running on AWS infrastructure.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: AWSSDK.Core underpins all AWS service clients.
Customize retry and timeout behavior via client config.
Prefer environment variables or IAM roles over hardcoded keys.
data.takeaway: AWSSDK.Core provides the foundation for reliable, configurable AWS service clients in .NET.

data.title: Exercise: Configure Retry Behavior
data.description: Create an S3 client with custom retry and timeout settings.
steps: Create an AmazonS3Config with MaxErrorRetry and Timeout.
Instantiate an AmazonS3Client with the config.
Print the client configuration to verify.
data.expectedOutcome: You can customize AWS client behavior for production scenarios.
